steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Consonant harmony sounds stable and restful; dissonant harmony sounds tense and unresolved — both are deliberate compositional choices. | Key Fact: Cadences are harmonic endings: perfect (V-I, final), plagal (IV-I, amen), imperfect (I-V or IV-V, unfinished), interrupted (V-vi, surprise). | Key Fact: Modulation changes the key centre: to the dominant (5th scale degree), subdominant (4th), or relative major/minor — each creates a different shift of mood. | Key Fact: Pedal notes are sustained or repeated while harmony changes above them — dominant pedals build tension; tonic pedals create stability.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe how harmony and tonality are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use harmony and tonality.
